hvtiRpropensity

Propensity score methods for cardiac surgery comparative-effectiveness research. Ports the balancing logic from SAS programs into a tidy R API whose outputs are compatible with hvtiPlotR and hvtiRutilities.

Status: the methods are implemented, and SAS parity is checked for the model fits and the CCF macros. Score estimation (ps_logistic(), ps_forest(), ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal(), bs_continuous(), bs_count()), the outcome-model bundles (fit_logistic(), fit_linear(), validate_logistic()), matching and weighting (ps_match(), ps_weight()), balance statistics (ps_stddiff(), ps_stddiff_perm(), ps_mw_var()), the support and survival summaries (ps_support(), ps_rmst()) and four sensitivity analyses (sa_rosenbaum(), sa_evalue(), sa_overlap(), sa_trim_sweep()) are exported and tested.

Since 0.1.10, tests compare the package against SAS 9.4 runs on synthetic fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/): the binary, ordinal and nominal logistic fits, the Poisson balancing score, fit_linear(), bs_continuous(), Rubin pooling against PROC MIANALYZE, and the CCF macros %stddiff, %stddiffci and %mw_var. Matching, weighting, ps_rmst(), ps_forest() and the sa_*() functions have no SAS oracle yet, so treat their agreement with SAS as unverified.

Full documentation: https://ehrlinger.github.io/hvtiRpropensity/

Installation 

# Install the development version from GitHub:
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ehrlinger/hvtiRpropensity")

Quick start 

library(hvtiRpropensity)

# Reproducible synthetic dataset. Drop the generator's true score so the
# example estimates its own.
dta <- sample_ps_data(n = 500, seed = 42)
dta$prob_t <- NULL

# --- Propensity score estimation ---
obj <- ps_logistic(tavr ~ age + female + ef + diabetes + hypertension, data = dta)

# --- 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching on the logit, caliper 0.2 SD ---
m <- ps_match(obj$data, score_col = "logit_t", scale = "logit",
              caliper_sd = 0.2, seed = 42)
print(m)
summary(m)
matched <- m$data[m$data$match == 1L, ]

# --- IPTW weighting (ATE) from the estimated score ---
w <- ps_weight(obj$data, estimand = "ATE")
print(w)
summary(w)

The caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit of the propensity score is the Austin (2011) recommendation. Give seed on every ps_match() call. Matching shuffles the order of the treated patients, and the seed makes the pairs reproducible.

Logistic model bundles

fit_logistic() fits binary, proportional-odds ordinal, and generalized-logit nominal outcome models. Clinically meaningful levels are always explicit; factor storage order never decides the event, order, or reference category.

binary_model <- fit_logistic(
  tavr ~ age + female + ef + diabetes + hypertension,
  data = dta,
  family = "binary",
  outcome_levels = c(0, 1),
  event_level = 1
)

Every model-producing result has four slots:

  • $data: patient-level data with predictions or scores;
  • $meta: formula, declared levels, model family, row accounting, package versions, and bundle_version = 1L;
  • $tables: estimates, covariance, by_imputation, and fit_status, plus workflow-specific diagnostics;
  • $models: every fitted model, including every imputation-specific fit.

The estimates table has columns term, estimate, std.error, statistic, df, p.value, conf.low, conf.high, odds_ratio, and pooled. Count models (bs_count()) name the exponentiated column rate_ratio, since a log-link coefficient exponentiates to a rate ratio. by_imputation has imputation, term, estimate, and std.error; fit_status has imputation, converged, n_input, n_analyzed, and n_excluded.

For stacked imputations, patient predictions are averaged across fits while coefficients and covariance use Rubin’s rules. Missing patients, changed categorical predictor levels, aliased terms, non-convergence, and unusable covariance matrices stop the analysis instead of producing a partial pool.

validate_logistic() applies a saved version-1 binary bundle to a declared validation cohort without refitting. It reports calibration, observed versus expected events, AUC, and Brier score. Ordinal and nominal validation are not part of this first interface.

Functions

Score estimation

Function Description
ps_logistic() Binary propensity score via logistic regression (with optional MI)
ps_forest() Binary propensity score from a random forest, out-of-bag (randomForestSRC)
ps_ordinal() Ordered treatment propensity via cumulative logit (MASS::polr)
ps_nominal() Nominal treatment propensity via generalised logit (nnet::multinom)
bs_continuous() Balancing score for continuous exposures via linear regression
bs_count() Balancing score for count exposures via negative-binomial or Poisson

Outcome models

Function Description
fit_logistic() Binary, ordinal, or nominal outcome-model bundle, with optional MI
fit_linear() Linear outcome-model bundle, with optional MI and Rubin pooling
validate_logistic() No-refit validation of a saved binary model bundle

Balancing methods

Function Description
ps_match() Greedy 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching, on the probability or logit scale, with an optional caliper (absolute or caliper_sd)
ps_weight() IPTW weighting for the ATE, ATT, or ATC estimand, optionally trimmed

Balance and treatment effects

Function Description
ps_stddiff() Standardized differences by variable type, optionally weighted (CCF %stddiff)
ps_stddiff_perm() Permutation reference for those differences (CCF %stddiffci)
ps_mw_var() Matching-weight difference in means with a bootstrap SD (CCF %mw_var)
ps_rmst() Restricted mean survival contrast, weighted or on matched pairs
ps_support() Compares common-support and trimming rules and how well they agree

Sensitivity analysis

Function Description
sa_rosenbaum() Rosenbaum gamma bounds for matched analyses (unmeasured confounding)
sa_evalue() E-values (VanderWeele & Ding 2017) for unmeasured confounding
sa_overlap() Overlap and positivity diagnostics on the score distribution
sa_trim_sweep() How effective sample size and weights move across IPTW trim thresholds

Utilities

Function Description
sample_ps_data() Synthetic cardiac-surgery dataset (binary treatment)
sample_ps_data_ordinal() Synthetic dataset with ordered treatment
sample_ps_data_nominal() Synthetic dataset with nominal treatment
sample_ps_data_count() Synthetic dataset with count exposure
is_ps_data() Predicate for ps_data objects

The four generators return plain data frames and is_ps_data() returns TRUE or FALSE. Every other export returns a ps_data object with $data, $meta and $tables.

Documentation

The Get started vignette walks the workflow from score to sensitivity analysis, including a worked example that reshapes the balance tables for hvtiPlotR::hv_balance().

The SAS programs this package ports ship with it: system.file("sas-templates", package = "hvtiRpropensity").

Related packages

  • hvtiPlotR: mirror histograms, balance plots, survival and hazard curves. hv_mirror_hist() reads the $data of a ps_match() or ps_weight() object directly. hv_balance() needs the SMD tables reshaped to long form in percent; the vignette shows how.
  • hvtiRutilities: data wrangling utilities for cardiac surgery datasets.
